data: The latest variant of the Orlan family — Russian rear-entry EVA suit, in service since the 1977 Salyut program

Latest generation of the Orlan rear-entry EVA suit family that began with Salyut 6 in 1977. The cosmonaut steps in through a backpack-mounted hatch that locks shut in one motion — no airlock pre-breathe gymnastics. Runs at 5.8 psi pure O₂, higher than the US EMU. Used on the ISS Russian segment.
The latest of a 50-year line of Russian rear-entry EVA suits

Latest variant of the Orlan family — Russian rear-entry EVA suit that has flown continuously since Salyut 6 in 1977. The cosmonaut steps in through a backpack-mounted hatch that locks shut in one motion, eliminating the airlock pre-breathe required by lower-pressure US suits. Operating pressure 5.8 psi (400 hPa) pure O₂. Used on the ISS Russian segment. Earlier Orlan variants served on Salyut and Mir stations.
